findings.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards silently drop any member whose `[Key]` value duplicates an earlier member's key, and no diagnostic is reported. Example: a public `[MessagePackObject]` class with `[Key(0)] int FirstValue` and `[Key(0)] int SecondValue`. On base this threw on `Dictionary.Add`: the generator failed visibly (CS8785) and the analyzer failed (AD0001). On head the generator emits a formatter that never reads or writes `SecondValue`, which is silent data loss, and the analyzer reports nothing. With SuppressSourceGeneration=true, the analyzer also stays silent even though DynamicObjectResolver rejects duplicate keys at runtime. The same applies to duplicate string keys (`stringMembers`) and to the second copy of the loop at lines 1173/1189. This also changes behaviour when SuppressSourceGeneration is unset, contrary to the acceptance criteria.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.DuplicateKeySilentlyDroppedTests.DuplicateIntKey_IsReportedOrSerialized. It drives MessagePackGenerator and all MessagePack analyzers over a type with two `[Key(0)]` properties. It asserts that either a MsgPack/CS8785/AD0001 diagnostic appears or the generated formatter references `SecondValue`. On head neither happens, so the test fails.
